title: Multimodal Retrieval & Fusion
description: Study joint and modality-specific indexes, late fusion and score calibration, missing and conflicting modalities, and multimodal retrieval evaluation. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Joint and modality-specific indexes
lessons.description: Design a query router for photos, serial numbers and mixed requests.
lessons.conceptOverview: A joint embedding space supports cross-modal retrieval, while separate indexes can preserve specialized signals such as exact OCR strings. Choose indexes by query needs and measure each modality's contribution.
lessons.whyItMatters: Different query types may require different retrieval signals.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A joint embedding space supports cross-modal retrieval, while separate indexes can preserve specialized signals such as exact OCR strings. Choose indexes by query needs and measure each modality's contribution.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: A joint embedding space supports cross-modal retrieval, while separate indexes can preserve specialized signals such as exact OCR strings. Choose indexes by query needs and measure each modality's contribution.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A product photo search benefits from visual similarity, while a serial-number query needs exact text matching.

sections.content: Design a query router for photos, serial numbers and mixed requests. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Different query types may require different retrieval signals.
commonMistakes: A single visual similarity index always handles exact identifiers well.

lessons.title: Late fusion and score calibration
lessons.description: Compare normalized-score fusion with reciprocal-rank fusion on a small labeled query set.
lessons.conceptOverview: Late fusion combines candidate rankings from multiple retrievers. Raw scores may have incompatible scales; rank-based fusion avoids assuming they are calibrated probabilities. Tune fusion on labeled relevance judgments.
lessons.whyItMatters: Raw scores from different retrievers are not automatically comparable.

sections.content: OCR search produces scores near 20 and image search scores near 0.8. Adding them directly makes text dominate regardless of relevance.

lessons.title: Missing and conflicting modalities
lessons.description: Create a response policy for absent, low-confidence and conflicting evidence.
lessons.conceptOverview: Real inputs can have missing images, noisy audio or contradictory text. Represent missingness explicitly and define an abstention or clarification policy instead of silently treating every source as equally reliable.
lessons.whyItMatters: Conflicting evidence should trigger explicit resolution or uncertainty.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A product label says 12 volts while a catalog entry says 24 volts. The assistant must expose the conflict instead of averaging the values.

lessons.title: Multimodal retrieval evaluation
lessons.description: Build a relevance rubric that includes revision identity and evidence sufficiency.
lessons.conceptOverview: Evaluate retrieval with modality-aware relevance labels and end-to-end answer support. A retrieved image may be visually similar yet unsuitable for a text question; separate recall, grounding and answer correctness.
lessons.whyItMatters: Visual resemblance is only one part of task relevance.
